name: ah
sound: Long like the a in "father", short like a clipped version of the same sound.
tip: Never the a in "cat". Keep the mouth open and the tongue low.

name: beh
sound: Like English b.
tip: At the end of a word it turns into p: gelb sounds like "gelp".

name: tseh
sound: Rare on its own. k in most words, ts before e and i.
tip: You will mostly meet it inside ch, sch and ck.

name: deh
sound: Like English d.
tip: At the end of a word it turns into t: Hund sounds like "hunt".

name: eh
sound: Long like "ay" in "day" but without the glide into y. Short like e in "bed". Unstressed at the end of a word like the a in "sofa".
tip: Final e is always spoken: bitte has two syllables.

name: eff
sound: Like English f.
tip: Same as English, nothing to fix here.

name: geh
sound: Always hard like g in "go", never like g in "gem".
tip: At the end of a word it turns into k (Tag sounds like "tahk"), and -ig at the end sounds like "ich".

name: hah
sound: Like English h at the start of a syllable.
tip: After a vowel it is silent and just makes the vowel long: gehen, die Kuh.

name: ee
sound: Long like ee in "see", short like i in "bit".
tip: Never the "eye" sound of English "I".

name: yot
sound: Like English y in "yes".
tip: Never the English j in "jam".

name: kah
sound: Like English k.
tip: Pronounced even before n: das Knie is "k-nee".

name: ell
sound: A light l with the tongue tip behind the top teeth.
tip: Avoid the dark l of English "full". German l stays bright in every position.

name: emm
sound: Like English m.
tip: Same as English.

name: enn
sound: Like English n.
tip: Same as English. ng is a single sound with no g after it.

name: oh
sound: Long like o in "go" but pure, with no glide into w. Short like o in British "hot".
tip: Round the lips and hold them still for the whole vowel.

name: peh
sound: Like English p.
tip: pf is two sounds said together: der Apfel.

name: koo
sound: Always in qu, which sounds like "kv".
tip: Never the "kw" of English "queen".

name: err
sound: Made at the back of the throat, close to a soft gargle.
tip: After a vowel or at the end of a word it melts into a short "uh": der, Mutter.

name: ess
sound: Before a vowel like English z, otherwise like s.
tip: sp and st at the start of a word sound like "shp" and "sht": der Sport, die Straße.

name: teh
sound: Like English t.
tip: Never flapped like the t in American "water".

name: oo
sound: Long like oo in "moon", short like u in "put".
tip: Never the "you" sound of English "use".

name: fow
sound: Usually like f.
tip: Some loanwords keep a v sound: die Vase, das Klavier.

name: veh
sound: Like English v.
tip: Never the English w. Touch the lower lip to the top teeth.

name: iks
sound: Like ks.
tip: Same as English x in "box".

name: üpsilon
sound: Mostly like ü in words from Greek, like y in some loanwords.
tip: Typ rhymes with "süß" more than with English "type".

name: tset
sound: Always ts, like the end of "cats".
tip: Never the English z in "zoo".

name: a-Umlaut
sound: Like e in "bed", often held longer.
tip: Often marks a plural: der Apfel, die Äpfel.

name: o-Umlaut
sound: Say "ay" (as in "day") and round your lips as if saying "oh".
tip: Tongue stays where e is, only the lips move.

name: u-Umlaut
sound: Say "ee" and round your lips tightly as if saying "oo".
tip: If it comes out as "oo", your tongue slid back. Keep it forward.

name: Eszett
sound: A sharp, voiceless s.
tip: Written after long vowels and au/ei/eu. After short vowels you write ss instead.
